title: Risk-Calibrated Predictive Link Adaptation Under Fast Fading with Feedback Delay: A Distributional Conformal Approach
content: Feedback and processing delays in time-varying wireless channels introduce severe mismatch between reported channel state information (CSI) and instantaneous channel realizations. When the feedback delay exceeds a non-negligible fraction of the channel coherence time (η = ∆/Tc), conventional link adaptation mechanisms either suffer from crippling spectral under-utilization or catastrophic block-error rate (BLER) violations. Although recurrent neural network predictors have been proposed to forecast future signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), conventional architectures provide deterministic point estimates that ignore aleatoric fading uncertainty. Consequently, under deep fades, point predictors recommend excessively aggressive modulation and coding schemes (MCS), resulting in severe quality-of-service (QoS) degradation. To overcome this fundamental limitation, we present a comprehensive risk-calibrated predictive link adaptation framework. The proposed method couples a probabilistic Gamma-parameterized gated recurrent unit (Gamma-GRU) predictor with distributional conformal calibration. By mapping calibrated predictive cumulative distributions onto physical modulation-and-coding thresholds, the transmitter quantifies the exact physical failure risk for each candidate MCS. We then allocate a dynamic reliability risk budget governed by a one-sided Wilson-score upper confidence bound (UCB) on empirical physical failure risk, ensuring conservative adaptation as uncertainty grows without requiring manual margin retuning. Through end-to-end coded simulations incorporating Clarke/Jakes flat-fading channels, rate-1/2 convolutional coding (K = 7), and soft-decision Viterbi decoding over 512-bit frames, we demonstrate that while deterministic point predictors and standard 3GPP outer-loop link adaptation (OLLA) suffer up to 28.6% and 13.3% mean BLER under long delays (η ≈ 2.01), the proposed policy maintains mean empirical BLER below the target 10% constraint across all evaluated horizons (0.48% to 8.17%). Simultaneously, it achieves up to a 2.3× goodput enhancement over conservative fixed fallbacks and maintains robustness across a 25× Doppler drift range (20 to 500 Hz) and unexpected Rician line-of-sight shifts. We explicitly frame this as an empirical upper confidence bound on physical failure probability, rather than a deterministic finite-sample SLA guarantee under non-exchangeable channel fading.
